entry.title: The AI Governance Gap: Why Most Enterprise Policies Are One Incident Behind
entry.summary: Every enterprise AI governance framework I've seen has the same structural flaw: it was written to prevent the last incident, not the next one. There's a pattern in enterprise AI governance that I've observed often enough to call it a rule. An organization deploys AI tools with minimal formal governance. Something goes wrong — a data exposure, a compliance finding, a public embarrassment, an internal incident where an AI agent did something nobody anticipated. The organization responds by writing a policy. The policy addresses exactly what happened. It says nothing about the seventeen related failure modes that share the same root cause. entry.title: Deep Inside the COM: Hunting the COM Global Interface Table (GIT)
entry.summary: If you've worked with classic Windows COM for any decent amount of time, you've almost certainly run into this frustrating reality: an interface pointer is not a universal passport. It works perfectly in the thread (apartment) where it was obtained, but hand it off to another thread and things quickly go south; crashes, deadlocks, and other mysterious failures. Both GUIDs belong to the classic OLE family — you can tell by the C000...46 ending.
